# Ultrasonic Thickness Inspection — PV-2201

Inspection date: 2026-08-12 · Unit: Crude Distillation · Inspector: P. Shetty

## Vessel

PV-2201 is a horizontal separator in hydrocarbon service, commissioned 2009,
nominal wall thickness 12.0 mm.

## Readings

Four ultrasonic readings were taken on the lower shell course. The governing
(lowest) measurement is 8.2 mm.

| Point | Thickness (mm) |
| ----- | -------------- |
| A     | 9.4            |
| B     | 8.9            |
| C     | 8.2            |
| D     | 9.1            |

## Observation

The governing measurement of 8.2 mm is below the minimum allowable thickness
for hydrocarbon service. External pitting was noted adjacent to point C.

## Condition of the shell course

The lower shell course shows general thinning consistent with the service
history of the vessel. Scattered external pitting is present over roughly one
third of the course, deepest adjacent to point C where the governing reading
was taken. No through-wall penetration was observed.

Internal inspection was not performed on this visit. The vessel was not opened,
so the internal surface condition is inferred from the ultrasonic readings
alone and from the previous internal inspection dated 2024-03-18.

## Insulation and coating

Insulation was removed at four points to permit measurement and reinstated on
completion. The vapour barrier was found intact at three of the four points. At
point C the barrier had failed, which is consistent with the pitting observed
there and is the most likely route for corrosion under insulation.

Coating over the inspected area is degraded and should be renewed at the next
opportunity regardless of the outcome of the thickness assessment.

## Prior readings

The previous ultrasonic inspection of this vessel was carried out on
2024-03-18. The governing reading at that time was 9.6 mm at point C, which was
above the minimum allowable thickness for hydrocarbon service.

## Notes for the assessor

This report records measurements only. It does not constitute a
fitness-for-service assessment, and no determination of remaining life has been
made here.
